chunks: Women are deficient in faith, deficient in shares and deficient in intelligence. As regards the deficiency in their faith, it is their abstention from prayers and fasting during their menstrual period. As regards deficiency in their intelligence it is because the evidence of two women is equal to that of one man. As for the deficiency of their shares that is because of their share in inheritance being half of men. So beware of the evils of women. Be on your guard even from those of them who are (reportedly) good. Do not obey them even in good things so that they may not attract you to evils.
ai.seo_question: What are the three deficiencies of women mentioned in Nahj al-Balagha and their corresponding jurisprudential proofs?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha, this passage categorizes women's 'shortcomings' (nuqsan) not as absolute deficits but as functional distinctions within Shia fiqh, linking specific legal rulings to faith, intellect, and status. The reference to testimony (shahada) for intellect and inheritance for status reflects classical juristic interpretations where these domains are seen as indicators of cognitive or social standing. The concluding ethical warning urges men to maintain balance, ensuring that women's compliance in obligatory acts does not lead to negligence in others, thereby preserving social order.
